title: Relational algebra and SQL
subtitle: Tables as sets, operators that build new sets — and SQL as the language that writes them down.

rel.title: Relations
rel.body: A relation is a table: columns are attributes, rows are tuples, and as a mathematical set it has no duplicate rows and no order. The running example has R(name, dept, salary) — four employees — and S(dept, building) — three departments. Every operator below takes relations and returns a relation.

sel.title: Select and project
sel.body: Selection σ keeps rows satisfying a condition: σsalary>45(R). Projection π keeps chosen columns and drops duplicate rows: πdept(R). In SQL: SELECT * FROM R WHERE salary > 45 and SELECT DISTINCT dept FROM R. Selection gives 2 rows here; projecting dept gives 3 (CS appears twice but only once in the set).

join.title: Joins
join.body: The Cartesian product R × S pairs every row with every row (12 rows here). A natural join R ⋈ S keeps only pairs that agree on the common attribute (dept) and merges the columns: 3 rows (Di’s department ME has no match, so she disappears). A left outer join keeps unmatched left rows, padding with NULL: 4 rows. SQL: SELECT * FROM R JOIN S ON R.dept = S.dept.

set.title: Set operations and aggregation
set.body: Union, intersection and difference need union-compatible tables (same columns). Aggregation collapses groups: SELECT dept, SUM(salary) FROM R GROUP BY dept gives CS:110 EE:40 ME:45. HAVING filters groups after aggregation, WHERE before it. Functions: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX.

sql.title: SQL: DDL, DML, views, triggers
sql.body: DDL defines structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP); DML manipulates data (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE); DCL controls access (GRANT, REVOKE). A view is a stored query that behaves like a table; a trigger runs automatically on an event; a stored procedure packages logic on the server. Nested subqueries: SELECT name FROM R WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM R).
sql.steps: Average salary in R is (50 + 40 + 60 + 45) / 4. Employees above it: Ann (50) and Cy (60).

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• σ rows, π columns, × all pairs, ⋈ matching pairs.
  • Outer joins keep unmatched rows with NULL.
  • GROUP BY aggregates; HAVING filters the groups.
